hints: Focus on how the size and polarising power of the Group 2 cation changes from Mg2+ to Ba2+ down the group.
Remember that larger, less polarising cations make carbonates and nitrates more stable to heat, so they need a higher temperature to decompose.
Compare the two solubility trends: hydroxides get more soluble down the group, so ask yourself which other solubility trend must go the opposite way.
walkthrough:
**Recall thermal stability down Group 2**

Think of a small Mg2+ ion as strongly polarising. It distorts the carbonate and nitrate ions and makes them easier to break apart.

Decomposition examples:
$$\text{MCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MO} + \text{CO}_2$$
$$2\text{M(NO}_3)_2 \rightarrow 2\text{MO} + 4\text{NO}_2 + \text{O}_2$$

**Link cation size to decomposition temperature**

Down the group from Mg2+ to Ba2+, the ion gets larger and its charge density falls. Polarising power decreases, so the carbonate and nitrate become more thermally stable.

Trend rule:
$$\text{larger cation} \rightarrow \text{less distortion} \rightarrow \text{higher decomposition temperature}$$

**Recall the two solubility trends**

This is a classic pair to learn together. Hydroxide solubility increases down the group, Mg(OH)2 is sparingly soluble while Ba(OH)2 is much more soluble.

In contrast, sulfate solubility decreases down the group, MgSO4 is very soluble while BaSO4 is essentially insoluble.

**Pick the decreasing property**

Decomposition temperatures increase, and hydroxide solubility increases. Only sulfate solubility shows a steady decrease from magnesium to barium.

options.A: Incorrect. Carbonates become more stable to heat down the group because the larger cation polarises the $\text{CO}_3^{2-}$ ion less. So the decomposition temperature increases from magnesium to barium, not decreases.
options.B: Incorrect. For the same reason as carbonates, nitrates become more stable to heat down the group. The decomposition temperature of $\text{Mg(NO}_3)_2$ is lower than that of $\text{Ba(NO}_3)_2$, so this trend increases.
options.C: Incorrect. Hydroxide solubility increases down Group 2. $\text{Mg(OH)}_2$ is only slightly soluble, while $\text{Ca(OH)}_2$, $\text{Sr(OH)}_2$ and $\text{Ba(OH)}_2$ become progressively more soluble.
options.D: Correct. Sulfate solubility decreases down Group 2. $\text{MgSO}_4$ is soluble, $\text{CaSO}_4$ is sparingly soluble, and $\text{SrSO}_4$ and $\text{BaSO}_4$ are insoluble. This is the only listed property that decreases from magnesium to barium.
